notes: WAR label = ewar_v2 through the war_source facade (bWAR/war_daily before the 2026-09-03 epoch), label_shape side_keyed_v1; absent target seasons score actual WAR 0 for model AND baseline

HISTORY, measured on the bWAR label of its day and SUPERSEDED IN SCOPE on 2026-09-03, when the facade default moved to ewar_v2 site-wide by owner decision: this gate now scores the eWAR label, so the smaller pitcher margin measured below is the expected shape of the current numbers, not a regression. eWAR LABEL SWAP MEASURED 2026-08-04 (lane R3b) and NOT ADOPTED then. Swapping the realized label to eWAR on the 6 fully covered targets (12,934 rows) makes the margin over the 5/4/3 carry-forward baseline SMALLER on pitchers, not larger: -0.0387 WAR against a pre-registered floor of +0.020, CI95 [-0.0472, -0.0309], negative in all six targets. THE TRAP IS WORTH NAMING because it will recur: the eWAR pitching label IS more forecastable (label r 0.5033 -> 0.5779, persistence 0.4528 -> 0.5823), so it is easy to read that as evidence for the swap. But this gate scores MARGIN OVER A PERSISTENCE BASELINE, and a 5/4/3 carry-forward IS a persistence bet, so a more persistent label helps the BASELINE more than it helps the model. A cleaner label raises the floor before it raises the ceiling. If eWAR is ever wired into the FA stack it needs a justification other than Gate 1, and Gate 1's floors would have to be re-derived on the new label.
